input.strategy_title: Reduce default workbench idle culling timeout to 8 hours
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

The default workbench idle culling timeout ships at 24 hours, so abandoned
workbenches hold GPUs overnight and through weekends. Fleet telemetry shows the
median idle-before-stop window admins actually configure is 8 hours. New
clusters should get the sensible default without an admin having to find the
setting.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters is 8 hours instead of 24. Existing clusters with an explicitly configured value are not changed on upgrade. |
| HLR-2 | P2 | The release note and cluster-settings documentation state the new default and how to override it. |

## Affected Components

- Notebooks
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- Per-project or per-user culling policies
- Changes to activity detection (kernel probe behavior)

## Open Questions

None — the setting, its ConfigMap, and the Dashboard administration UI already
exist; only the shipped default changes.

# Change default workbench idle culling timeout to 8 hours

## Description

This epic delivers the core change of the strategy: newly installed clusters
ship with a default workbench idle culling timeout of 8 hours instead of 24,
while existing clusters that have an explicitly configured value keep their
configuration on upgrade. The idle culling setting, its ConfigMap
(`notebook-controller-culler-config`), and the Dashboard administration UI
already exist; this epic changes only the shipped default value and the logic
that decides when the default is applied versus when an existing explicit value
is preserved.

## Scope

- Change the shipped default value of the workbench idle culling timeout from
  24 hours to 8 hours in the Dashboard's culling configuration handling
  (OdhDashboardConfig notebookController settings that render the culler
  configuration).
- Ensure fresh installs receive the 8-hour default with no admin action
  required.
- Ensure upgrade logic does not overwrite an explicitly configured idle culling
  timeout on clusters that already set one; clusters relying on the previous
  default (no explicit value) move to the 8-hour default.
- Update any admin-facing display of the default value in the Dashboard
  administration UI (placeholders, hints, help text) so it reflects 8 hours.
- Update/extend unit coverage for the defaulting logic and the
  upgrade-preservation logic.

Out of scope: per-project/per-user culling policies and any change to activity
detection (kernel probe behavior), per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a newly installed cluster with no admin configuration, when a workbench
  is provisioned, then the idle culling timeout default is 8 hours.
- Given a cluster upgraded from a previous release with an explicitly
  configured idle culling timeout, when the upgrade completes, then the
  explicitly configured value is unchanged.
- Given a cluster upgraded from a previous release with no explicit value
  (relying on the old 24-hour default), when the upgrade completes, then the
  effective idle culling timeout is 8 hours.
- Given an admin needs the previous behavior, when they explicitly configure
  the idle culling timeout, then the explicit value takes precedence over the
  default (documented rollback/override path — no feature flag needed since the
  override mechanism already exists).
- Unit tests covering the defaulting, upgrade-preservation, and override
  precedence logic pass in the component's CI/build pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters is
  8 hours instead of 24. Existing clusters with an explicitly configured value
  are not changed on upgrade.

# Validate workbench culling behavior with the 8-hour default timeout

## Description

This epic validates that the workbench idle culler — which requires no code
change for this strategy — operates correctly once the shipped default idle
culling timeout changes to 8 hours. The culler is owned by the Workbenches
team, a different team than the one implementing the default change, so this
validation is scoped as its own epic rather than an acceptance criterion on the
implementing epic. The deliverable is validation evidence that the new default
behaves as intended end-to-end and that existing override behavior is
unaffected.

## Scope

- Validate that workbenches idle beyond the new 8-hour default are stopped by
  the culler on a cluster running the new default.
- Validate that workbenches with kernel activity inside the window are not
  culled (activity detection via Jupyter server API kernel probes continues to
  work unchanged).
- Validate that explicitly configured idle culling timeouts (admin-set or
  per-workbench overrides) take precedence over the new default after upgrade.
- Validate that no regression is introduced in culling behavior for
  StatefulSet-backed workbenches (workbenches stop and restart cleanly when
  culled).
- Produce a validation report summarizing scenarios, environment, and results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a cluster with the new default and a workbench idle for the configured
  threshold, when the culling check runs, then the workbench is stopped.
- Given a cluster with the new default and a workbench with recent kernel
  activity, when the culling check runs, then the workbench is not culled.
- Given a cluster with an explicitly configured idle culling timeout, when
  culling evaluates that workbench, then the explicit value is honored rather
  than the 8-hour default.
- A validation report exists documenting the scenarios executed and their
  results, including any issues found and their disposition.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters is
  8 hours instead of 24. Existing clusters with an explicitly configured value
  are not changed on upgrade. (This epic provides the Workbenches-team
  validation of culler behavior under the new default.)

# Document the 8-hour default idle culling timeout and how to override it

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for the new default: the release note and
the cluster-settings documentation state that the default workbench idle
culling timeout is now 8 hours (previously 24), and explain how administrators
override it. This is substantive documentation content work following the Red
Hat docs content process, scoped separately from the code change.

## Scope

- Update the cluster-settings documentation to state the new 8-hour default
  idle culling timeout for workbenches.
- Document how administrators override the default (explicit idle culling
  timeout configuration through the Dashboard administration UI /
  OdhDashboardConfig notebookController settings).
- Call out the upgrade behavior in the release note: explicitly configured
  clusters are unchanged; clusters relying on the old 24-hour default move to
  8-hour culling on upgrade, with the override path for admins who need the
  previous behavior.
- Ensure documented values and override instructions match the implemented and
  validated behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The release note states the new 8-hour default, the change from the previous
  24-hour default, and the override path.
- The cluster-settings documentation states the new default and step-by-step
  override instructions.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  and validation results before publication.
- Documentation accuracy is validated against the architecture context for the
  affected components (culling administered through Dashboard
  OdhDashboardConfig notebookController settings; culler reads the
  `notebook-controller-culler-config` ConfigMap).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P2): The release note and cluster-settings documentation state the new
  default and how to override it.
